Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 38
  gender: Female
  ethnicity: African
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Fisherman
  trauma_type: Trauma to a loved one
  pcl5: 76

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Anniversaries: The anniversary of the event, Crash Discussions: Talk about accidents, Crash Imagery: Cars hit by accident
  Maladaptive Strategies: Prevention Rumination: I dwell on how the event could have been prevented, Compulsive Spending: I spend money impulsively to distract or comfort myself, Delay Sleep: stay up until very late
  Threat: Negative Emotions: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame, Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience, Irritability: Irritable behavior, angry outbursts, or acting aggressively
  Negative Appraisals: Inaction Guilt: I will never forgive myself for not doing more to stop what happened, Self-Blame: The event happened because of the way I acted, Failed to Protect: I should have protected others and I failed

Vignette:
Emma, a 38-year-old African woman married with two children, has been struggling since the tragic loss of her brother, who died in a car accident five years ago. The event occurred on a rainy night when he was returning home from work. Emma had come to believe that if she had insisted on driving him or offered to stay up later to accompany him, his life might have been saved. This belief has fueled a relentless cycle of rumination and self-blame. On the anniversary of her brother’s death, Emma found herself overwhelmed by memories. The day was marked with silence and solitude as she dwelled on how different things could be if only she had taken action sooner. She would often find herself replaying that fateful night in her mind—every twist and turn of events leading to his untimely demise. This intense focus on prevention ruminations kept her restless, unable to sleep until very late at night. Emma’s work as a fisherman exposed her to numerous triggers. One day, while discussing a recent fishing accident with colleagues, she felt an overwhelming surge of fear and horror wash over her. Her heart raced, and she broke into a cold sweat. The physical reactivity was so intense that it left her feeling weak and anxious for the rest of the day. She found herself irritable and short-tempered with her coworkers, unable to shake off the emotions that threatened to engulf her. In an attempt to manage these overwhelming feelings, Emma turned to impulsive spending as a coping mechanism. She would buy things she didn’t need—luxury items or unnecessary gadgets—just to distract herself from the pain and guilt she carried. This behavior led to mounting debts and financial strain, which further exacerbated her stress and anxiety. Emma’s marriage has also been affected by these struggles. Her husband noticed that she had become distant and irritable, often snapping at him over minor issues. He tried to be understanding but found it increasingly difficult to navigate the emotional turmoil she was experiencing. Emma felt a deep sense of guilt for burdening her husband with her pain, which only deepened her negative appraisals and self-blame. Despite her efforts to cope, the anniversary of her brother’s death continues to be especially challenging. She avoids going out or engaging in activities that remind her of him. Instead, she spends time alone, ruminating on what could have been done differently. This isolation has led her to feel increasingly disconnected from those around her. What finally brought Emma to seek help was the realization that these patterns were not only harming her but also affecting her family and work life. She had come to believe that if she didn’t address these issues, they would continue to deteriorate further. Emma is most afraid of being trapped in a cycle of guilt and self-blame, unable to forgive herself or move forward from this loss. She hopes to find ways to process her emotions and regain control over her life, aiming for a sense of peace and understanding that will allow her to heal and reconnect with those around her. Emma’s journey towards recovery is marked by an earnest desire to confront the pain she carries and learn healthier coping mechanisms to navigate through it.
